base.description: CRS326-24S+2Q+RM - 24 SFP+ cages, two QSFP+ cages, the management and boot jack, the RJ45 console and a USB type A port. The box holds two IEC cords, rack ears and the K10 screw and feet kit.

description: MikroTik CRS326-24S+2Q+RM is a fixed 1U Cloud Router Switch. It has 24 SFP+ cages and two 40G QSFP+ cages. It also has a 10/100 management and boot port, an RJ45 serial console and a USB type A port. It runs RouterOS or SwOS. The front carries the 24 SFP+ cages in three blocks of four columns by two rows. They are numbered 1 to 24 as printed, with the odd number on the lower cage of a column. The two QSFP+ cages are 1 and 2, stacked with the odd number below. Right of them are the CONSOLE and MGMT/BOOT jacks, the RESET button, the USB port and the USER, FAULT, PWR 2 and PWR 1 lamps. The rear carries two AC inlets (POWER 1 and POWER 2, 100-240 V) and three fans. The power supplies and the fans are built into the chassis, so there are no bays.

ac-input-rating.note: Each inlet prints "100-240 V ~1 A MAX 50/60 Hz" under POWER 1 or POWER 2 (photograph 1832); the brochure's range is 100 - 240 V.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: The product page lists two AC inputs, two PSU slots and "3 fans"; the quick guide says "Two integrated power supply units with AC inputs for redundancy" and "Three cooling fans with automatic speed control"; the brochure lists "Redundant supply: Yes" and two IEC cords in the box. The rear photograph shows a plain panel with the two inlets on it and no removable module, and no held document prints a supply module part number, so the supplies are built in: part of the chassis, not bays. The three round openings of the rear have a fan behind each, so they are fans of the chassis.

chassis.note: 443 wide, 44.45 high (the brochure's "44" is the 1U pitch, 44.45), 200 deep: the brochure's and the product page's one source for the depth, both "443 x 200 x 44 mm". No drawing is held, so no figure is checked against one. 443 is the body between the ear folds.

colour.note: The pilot's face (#dadada) is carried; the studio render is lit differently.

datasheet.note: The brochure is MikroTik's datasheet for the model: QCA9531 CPU at 650 MHz, 128 MB RAM, 32 MB flash, one 10/100 port, 24 SFP+ and two QSFP+ cages, RouterOS or SwitchOS (licence level 5), AC supply 100 - 240 V, "Redundant supply: Yes", USB type A, serial RJ45, 443 x 200 x 44 mm, -20 to +60 C, "Max power consumption" 69 W. The page adds the switch chip 98DX8332, two AC inputs, two PSU slots, three fans, 42 W without attachments and a 1 A USB limit. The 69 W is unqualified and filed as the maximum; the quick guide says "up to 42 W. With attachments up to 69 W", which agrees.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (brochure and product page, Included: Rack ears; Screw and feet kit K10). No drawing is held, so no position is dimensioned: the shipped position is taken as flush, as on the other CRS in the library, and the ears are not drawn.

front-layout.note: estimated - read off photograph 1831 as gate-1 says. Three cage blocks of four columns by two rows at 15.7, 78.9 and 142.1 mm (63.2 mm apart), the cage pitch 14.37 mm, the QSFP+ block 19.8 mm wide at 207.0 mm, the CONSOLE and MGMT/BOOT block 17.6 mm wide at 232.1 mm. Each cage column's lamp strip shows four arrows; they are drawn as two lamps for each cage, as the CRS354 drawing shows.

gate-1.note: estimated - the front photograph 1831 (3000 x 1200 px) shows the face between the ear folds 1685 px across in the 2000 px view for the printed 443 (3.805 px per mm) and 164 px between the ears' top and bottom edges for 44.45 (3.69 px per mm): 3 percent apart, so the picture is not orthographic enough to call photo-measured. x is taken at 3.805 px per mm from the body's left edge and y at 3.66 px per mm from the face's top edge. The cage pitch then reads 14.37 mm against the registry's 14.25 for a ganged SFP cage, 0.8 percent apart. Every position is good to about 1 mm in x and 1.5 mm in y.

lamps.note: Four lamps right of the USB port, top to bottom USER (green), FAULT (red), PWR 2 (blue) and PWR 1 (blue), as printed beside them. No document held says what a lamp shows (the brochure and the quick guide give no LED table, only that the reset button works with "a green LED"), so none carries states beyond the component's own.

port-numbering.note: Printed numbers in photograph 1831: 2 4 6 ... 24 above the upper row and 1 3 5 ... 23 below the lower row, 40G QSFP+ 2 above and 1 below, CONSOLE above the upper right jack and MGMT/BOOT below the lower. The brochure's one 10/100 port is the MGMT/BOOT jack; the serial console is the CONSOLE jack.

rear-layout.note: estimated - no rear elevation is held; the positions are read off the studio rear photograph 1832. It looks down on the rear, so x is taken at 4.036 px per mm across the 443 mm body and y is estimated at 2.9 px per mm. They are good to about 2 mm in x and 3 mm in y. As seen from the rear: the inlets centred at 29.0 and 113.7 mm with POWER 1 and POWER 2 above their rating legends, and three fans 35 mm across at 225.2, 267.4 and 336.2 mm. The fans' corner screws and the wire retaining loops over the inlets are not drawn (the loops are accessories).

reset.note: RESET is a round button between the MGMT/BOOT jack and the USB port; the quick guide's reset section says to hold it at power-up until the LED flashes.
